title: prefix sums, difference arrays, and static range queries
concepts: A prefix aggregate stores the cumulative result from the start through each position.
A leading identity value makes half-open range queries easier to express and prevents special handling at the first index.
For addition, a range sum is the difference between two prefix sums; this answers static queries in constant time after linear preprocessing.
Prefix sums remain valid only while the underlying array is static; interleaved updates and queries need another data structure.
A prefix-frequency map counts target-sum subarrays even when elements may be negative, where a shrinking sliding window is not monotone.
Prefix remainders support divisibility counts when equal remainders delimit a sum divisible by the modulus.
Two-dimensional prefix sums use inclusion-exclusion to answer rectangular sum queries from four precomputed corners.
A difference array is the discrete inverse of prefix accumulation and converts a range increment into two boundary changes.
After all offline range updates, one prefix pass reconstructs the final values; reading intermediate values requires a different structure.
Choose prefix aggregates for repeated static queries and difference arrays for offline range updates, while checking index conventions and accumulator overflow.
